newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Reinvigorated dollar climbs, G7 ends worries.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Reinvigorated dollar climbs, G7 ends worries.

text.p: The dollar climbed steeply on Monday, reinvigorated by comments from finance ministers of the G7 industrialised countries which removed market worries about the strength of the U.S. currency.

On European equity markets, the morning session was lacklustre. London and Paris edged ahead slightly in trading that was dominated by upcoming general elections while the stronger dollar and prospects of cheaper exports helped some Frankfurt stocks.

The dollar rallied in early trade to a 37-month high against the mark and near its 55-month peak against the yen before easing slightly at midday as the bullish mood triggered triggered by Sunday's G7 meeting cooled .
But traders said a pause for breath was only natural after the dollar's sprint forward.
"The dollar's been well-bid all morning. Most people think this is a reasonable level to buy dollars after the G7 made them feel quite comfortable about buying it," said one trader at a British bank.
The dollar soared after the G7 ministers said major currency misaligments had been corrected and that excessive currency volatility and deviations from fundamentals were undesirable.
Analysts said the remarks lacked aggressiveness and had made dollar bulls comfortable.

The dollar was at 1.7316 marks by lunchtime , off the overnight high of 1.7395, and against 1.7235 in late European trade on Friday. It was at 126.77 yen, off a peak of 127.10 but up from its pre-G7 Friday level of 125.92.

The market view in the light of the G7 statement appeared to be that the authorities would tolerate a strong dollar as long as it did not move rapidly, analysts said, citing a remark made by Bank of England Governor Eddie George after the meeting.
George said G7 officials felt the foreign exchange environment was "in pretty good shape" and that no need had been expressed at the meeting for an action plan to deal with future currency moves.
But euphoria was clouded because the G7 had sounded a warning note on trade imbalances.

The meeting emphasised the importance of avoiding currency moves that could lead to a re-emergence of large trade imbalances. They named no names, but markets saw this as a reference to Japan's swelling, politically sensitive trade surplus with the U.S.
In equity markets, French stocks lost some of their early gains made after two polls gave the ruling centre-right coalition a sizeable majority in the upcoming parliamentary election.
A poll published in Monday's Le Figaro saw the centre-right winning the May 25-June 1 election with 329 seats, with the Socialists, other left and ecologists obtaining 202.

Another poll published on Sunday also showed the RPR-UDF coalition and conservative allies winning. The two polls were expected to provide some reassurance for the French financial markets, which were jolted last week by a poll predicting a tight race.
But the bourse's advance was muted by caution ahead of a string of U.S. economic indicators due out this week, brokers said, and the CAC-40 index was only just in the plus column by midday.
London shares moved ahead only slightly, with the market weighed down by New York's 0.79 percent losses on Friday and political uncertainty over the outcome of Thursday's UK election.
Talk of an interest rate rise next week of as much as a half point next week also depressed investors.
Dealers also said markets were likely fret over U.S. figures this week -- culminating in the key employment report on Friday -- which could renew fears of a rise in U.S. interest rates.
In Frankfurt, the picture was mixed with floor trade slipping 0.3 percent but deals on the computerised IBIS index making modest gains, boosted by the dollar.
STOCKS AT 1130 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 7.6 points at 4,377.3.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 4.9 points at 2,541.16.
Frankfurt's DAX index was down 11. 04 at 3363.06.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7316 against the mark versus 1.7235 in late European trade on Friday. Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 126.77 from 125.92.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was at fixed at $341.25 ounce after ending at $342.45 in London on Friday. Silver unchanged at was at $4.73.
